incidents.name: MEV bot 0x0000...a47b unguarded callback
incidents.notes: The arbitrage bot's callback entry point performed no caller check and read the target address out of attacker-supplied calldata, so the attacker made it move its own USDC balance to a contract they controlled.

sources.ref: onchain review: bot 0x00000000000a47b1298f18cf67de547bbe0d723f created 2022-04-01T10:59:44Z by 0x4239dff29d9b526688b0062e8ee79bb8b439b123, unrelated to the attack sender 0x1dc90b5b...; unverified but non-upgradeable, no EIP-1967 events, age from deployment. 187.75 WETH x $1,290.89 at incidentTimestamp 1665689975 (DefiLlama) = $242,364.

re-check 2026 (deployment-basis rows with a DELEGATECALL in the runtime): CORRECTION - the earlier note that the bot is 'non-upgradeable' is wrong. The address is a CREATE2 slot that its operator 0xdc3c2c78ef0e11952af23dccd8e24a0a64c9d20e self-destructs and redeploys: bisecting eth_getCode over [14499949, 15741333] finds 9 distinct runtimes and Etherscan txlistinternal lists 17 create/create2 records for the address in that window, the last at block 15532252, 2022-09-14T09:46:31Z (tx 0x51819d7c8ed4df00e5869c63e80955b7f1d13bf2f7435bb0474a08864d73096e). The code running at the incident is the one deployed then (byte-identical from block 15532252 through 15741333), not the 2022-04-01 original. Age 1665689975 - 1663148791 = 2,541,184 s (29.4 d), was 16,879,191 s (195.4 d). Separately, callTracer on the exploit tx shows the bot delegatecalling two caller-supplied targets (0x770200a211315a0688c289f437317ea117cb4d23, 0xfbc83fa919e6c83d9d9ccc1171df44d624da4c25), which is the unguarded entry point itself rather than an upgrade mechanism.

incidents.documentedLastChange: 2022-09-14T09:46:31Z (block 15532252, tx 0x51819d7c8ed4df00e5869c63e80955b7f1d13bf2f7435bb0474a08864d73096e): last CREATE2 redeployment of 0x00000000000a47b1298f18cf67de547bbe0d723f by 0xdc3c2c78ef0e11952af23dccd8e24a0a64c9d20e before the incident; the address had been self-destructed and recreated 17 times since 2022-04-01
